newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-NASHVILLE, ATLANTA, ST. PAUL, COLUMBUS TO GET FRANCHISES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-NASHVILLE, ATLANTA, ST. PAUL, COLUMBUS TO GET FRANCHISES.

text.p: Nashville, Tennessee, Atlanta, St. Paul, Minnesota and Columbus, Ohio were tabbed by the National Hockey League's Expansion Committee on Tuesday as the league's next four expansion franchises.
The NHL's Board of Governors will put the recommendation by the expansion committee to a vote at a meeting in New York on June 25. A three-fourths vote is required for admission of new members.
Each of the new franchises would pay an $80 million francise fee, the league said. The suggested expansion would boost NHL membership to 30 teams.
The Nashville franchise would begin play in the 1998-99 season, followed by Atlanta in 1999-2000, and St. Paul and Columbus in 2000-01, according to the proposal.

As part of the expansion plan, the NHL and the NHL Players' Association have agreed to a four-year extension to the collective bargaining agreement, subject to ratification, that extends it until September 15, 2004, the league said.
The committee also recommends a new alignment for the league, that would ultimately see two conferences, each comprised of three divisions of five teams.

The league already has added five teams this decade. The San Jose Sharks entered the NHL in 1990. The Tampa Bay Lightning and Ottawa Senators began play in 1991 and the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim and Florida Panthers joined the league two years later.
